content: The image shows a soybean stem close-up at a node with what appears to be grayish-white fluffy/cottony growth at the node junction, with yellowed leaves. Let me view reference images for my top candidates.

Based on my analysis, the grayish-white cottony/fluffy growth at the stem node with yellowed leaves is most consistent with **White_Mold**. That's my initial prediction.

Now let me check the attractor guide per the protocol.
White_Mold is flagged as over-predicted (20x wrong), with Phomopsis (6x) being the top confusion. Let me check the Phomopsis reference.

Phomopsis shows infected pods/seeds with gray mold and cracking - this doesn't match the test image which shows a stem node with cottony growth.

The test image clearly shows:
- Green soybean stem at a node
- Grayish-white fluffy/cottony mycelial growth at the node junction
- Yellowed leaves surrounding the plant
- The stem itself is still green but the node has distinctive fuzzy white mold growth

This matches the White_Mold description perfectly: "fluffy white mold growth on soybean stems... gray to white lesions at nodes... leaves turn gray-green then brown." The White_Mold reference images confirm the same pattern of white mycelial growth at stem nodes.

None of the attractor alternatives match: Phomopsis is about seed/pod symptoms, Tobacco_Streak_Virus shows pod lesions and bud blight, Charcoal_Rot shows internal microsclerotia, Diaporthe shows linear black pycnidia on stems, and Anthracnose shows dark lesions with black fruiting bodies.
